BiblicalUsage: The word appears once: Festus tells Agrippa that when Paul's accusers came to Caesarea, 'without any delay on the morrow I sat on the judgment seat, and commanded the man to be brought forth.' It is a putting off — and here the point is that there was none. Festus moved at once, and Paul's case came before the king.
TheologicalSignificance: One word for delay carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the contrast — Festus did not delay, and the gospel got its hearing before Agrippa the same week.
